commits.edited_message:
Harden MCOS metadata parsing

Compute dimension products with the overflow-checked helpers and reject
empty dimension lists.

Object metadata written by some third-party writers stores fewer object
ids than the declared dimensions call for. Keep the declared rank and
dims and read as many ids as are present, taking the class id after the
last id instead of discarding the variable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bound MCOS cell array walks to the allocated size

The cell dimensions come from the subsystem metadata and can disagree
with the number of pointers actually stored in matvar->data, so walk
only what was allocated.

The resolved object field walk needs no such clamp: ResolveMCOS
allocates num_fields * num_objects field pointers, which is exactly the
set of elements stored for the object.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is an out-of-bounds heap read in ResolveNestedMCOS (src/mcos.c, MAT_C_OBJECT/MAT_C_STRUCT branch) that walks total = num_fields * product(dims) matvar_t* slots over data allocated by ResolveMCOS as num_fields * num_objects pointers. Neither edited commit is unsafe by itself; the bug only appears when both edits are read together. Commit e9a020a ('Harden MCOS metadata parsing') relaxes ParseOpaqueMetadata: instead of requiring the opaque metadata to hold one object id per declared dimension element (obj_start + total_objs < meta_nvals), it accepts a truncated id list, clamps num_objects to the ids actually stored, and keeps the declared rank/dims. A variable may therefore carry dims 5x1 (product 5) with num_objects 1. This is benign on its own: with the later clamps in place every consumer that indexes by dims is bounded to the allocation. Commit e670d4f ('Bound MCOS cell array walks to the allocated size') adds the ParseSubsystem5 cell-count guard and the ResolveNestedMCOS cell-branch clamp, but its edit omits the struct/object-branch clamp that the real commit adds, on the stated reasoning that ResolveMCOS allocates exactly num_fields * num_objects field pointers. That reasoning only holds while num_objects equals the product of dims - the invariant the first edited commit relaxed. Read alone, each diff is plausible maintenance: the first is a robustness change for third-party writers, the second keeps its bound for cell arrays and its commit message documents the allocation invariant it relies on. The proof of-contract input is a MAT5 file whose MCOS opaque variable declares dims 5x1 with a single stored object id and a one-property class; ResolveMCOS builds a 1-pointer field array while the variable keeps dims 5x1, and the unclamped walk reads fields[1..4] past the 8-byte allocation (verified: ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ, SIGABRT). A correct fix is necessarily non-local: restoring e670d4f's struct-branch clamp alone heals the walk, and restoring e9a020a's strict id-list acceptance alone leaves the variable opaque - either single-commit fix removes the reachable bug only by re-establishing the dims<->num_objects invariant that the two commits jointly broke, so the reviewer must reason about both diffs (the producer ParseOpaqueMetadata and the consumer ResolveNestedMCOS/ResolveMCOS) to see why the walk count and the allocation count diverge. Variant runs on the tip tree confirm delocalization: with only the e9a020a edit applied (clamps intact) the file resolves to a MAT_C_OBJECT and exits cleanly; with only the e670d4f edit applied (strict acceptance intact) the variable is left opaque and exits cleanly; only the composition aborts. The pristine batch (d8e54c5) and main are likewise clean, so the base is secure and the regime is new_defect.

pocs.entry_point: public API <matio.h>: Mat_Open(MAT_ACC_RDONLY) + Mat_VarRead(mat, "mcosvar") + Mat_VarFree + Mat_Close on a crafted uncompressed MAT5 file written to a temp path
